messages.author: 651082d49f5d09de
messages.subject: Comparing 2 SWC files
parts:
Is there a way in R to use NBLAST to take two SWC files and compare them for similarity (possibly outputing some sort of similarity score)?

Thanks for your help,
Corey Elowsky

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Comparing 2 SWC files
parts:
Dear Corey,

This a pretty standard operation at this point. See docs for read.neurons to bring in the SWC files, dotprops to convert them into the format used by nblast or nblast_allbyall

See https://github.com/natverse/nat.examples and 

https://github.com/natverse/nat.nblast

For more information.

The main issue is the spatial scale of your neurons. NBLAST v2 is tuned for drosophila neurons. You either need to rescale your neurons to match or choose a different scoring procedure. 

Best,

Greg. 

Sent from my iPhone

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Comparing 2 SWC files
parts:
> On 4 Mar 2020, at 21:10, Corey Elowsky <coreye...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I notice that when I compare 2 SWC's using nblast and swap the query and target, the output similarity score is very different. Is this the expected behavior?

If the neurons are very different sizes, then yes. NBLAST scores are not symmetric. See the NBLAST paper for details.

You can ask for normalised scores, but there will still be an asymmetry if you are comparing a big neuron to a small one and vice versa.

Best,

Greg.
